extracted.intended_audience: creative writers (fiction), writers seeking revision and craft guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft and revision guidance for fiction writers on how to handle rough patches, revise toward clarity, and generate plot from character. Focuses on mindset, revision practices, and how to read your own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reframe problems as potential
rubrics_metrics.description: A rough patch in a story is not an error or a defect or evidence of our lack of talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat rough patches as "avoidance moments" where the subconscious is working through something important; view them as opportunities rather than failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories develop in waves (expect multiple drafts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A good story occurs in waves; a piece typically requires numerous drafts before reaching final form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept imperfection at intermediate stages as normal and productive — revision is part of the story's natural unfolding rather than merely polishing a finished object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice active waiting
rubrics_metrics.description: When you encounter unclear moments, the solution isn't immediate fixing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep revising the section and surrounding material "with affection and hope, until it relents and pops into clarity" — persistently work and wait rather than forcing a premature solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat problematic passages as load-bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Confusing spots often contain the story's core identity; approach them "like a future all-star."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume that passages giving trouble are important because they carry significant potential; prioritize and protect them rather than cutting or dismissing them as dispensable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize interconnected problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoidance moments operate as "a co-dependent system" — solving one often helps resolve others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for patterns and relationships among difficulties; address clusters of issues (tone, character, scene) rather than treating each glitch in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision method: read with a P/N meter and outsider perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Saunders imagines a meter with "P" (Positive) and "N" (Negative) and reads his story the way he would read someone else's, noting honest reactions before editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the reader's perspective and mark genuine positive and negative reactions as you read; resist immediate defensive editing so you can gather accurate signals about what works and what doesn't.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make thousands of micro-decisions guided by intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision consists of many "micro-decisions" that are intuitive: simply preferring one thing to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust small, habitual judgments accumulated over many passes rather than trying to invent wholesale fixes; these incremental choices move the piece toward coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate plot through detailed character work
rubrics_metrics.description: If I make a person in enough detail, this creates plot. If you make a vivid, funny person that the reader feels some connection with, anything that happens to that person is going to feel meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize creating richly detailed, distinctive characters; let character specificity and the reader's emotional connection drive events so plot emerges organically from character rather than being imposed externally.
